seo.title: Guayaquil's Pacific Seafood (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Dive into Guayaquil's vibrant seafood scene! Discover the top 12 restaurants for ceviche, encebollado, and fresh Pacific catches, from iconic street food to upscale dining.

hero.subtitle: Guayaquil, the Pearl of the Pacific, boasts a culinary scene deeply rooted in its access to fresh ocean bounty. From zesty ceviches to hearty encebollados, the city's seafood is a vibrant reflection of its coastal heritage.

picks.name: Caracol Azul
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Guayaquil institution since 1978, Caracol Azul is synonymous with upscale, traditional Ecuadorian seafood. Known for its impeccable service and elegant atmosphere, it's the perfect place for a special occasion or to savor classic dishes prepared with fresh, high-quality ingredients. The decor evokes a classic maritime feel.
picks.whatToOrder: Langosta a la Termidor (Thermidor Lobster) or Arroz con Camarones (Shrimp Rice)
picks.insiderTip: Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends. It's a great spot to try traditional Ecuadorian wines and spirits.
picks.redditQuote: "Caracol Azul is worth every penny. Had the best lobster of my life there, the service was amazing. Definitely a 'must-do' for fancy seafood in GYE."

picks.name: La Pata Gorda
picks.whyItMadeTheList: La Pata Gorda is a lively and popular spot famous for its generous portions and wide array of fresh ceviches. With multiple locations, it's a go-to for locals seeking vibrant flavors and a buzzing atmosphere. Their ceviche varieties, from traditional to more elaborate concoctions, are a true highlight.
picks.whatToOrder: Ceviche Mixto (Mixed Ceviche) or Arroz Marinero (Sailor's Rice)
picks.insiderTip: Go early for lunch or dinner to avoid the busiest crowds, especially on weekends. Their spicy sauce is a game-changer, but use with caution!
picks.redditQuote: "You HAVE to try La Pata Gorda for ceviche. Seriously, their mixed ceviche is enormous and so fresh. It's always packed for a reason."

picks.name: Pique y Pase
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A historic and beloved spot in the heart of Guayaquil, Pique y Pase offers authentic, home-style Ecuadorian seafood at very reasonable prices. It's a no-frills, bustling eatery perfect for an immersive local lunch experience. Their daily specials feature seasonal catches and traditional preparations.
picks.whatToOrder: Encebollado (Fish Stew) or Seco de Chivo (Goat Stew - seafood alternative available)
picks.insiderTip: This place gets incredibly busy during lunch hours. Be prepared to share a table or wait, but the food is worth it. Cash is preferred.
picks.redditQuote: "For a truly local feel and cheap, delicious encebollado, Pique y Pase is my absolute favorite. It's a Guayaquil staple."

picks.name: Mariscos de la 29
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An iconic, bustling street food experience that locals swear by. Mariscos de la 29 is not a single restaurant but a collection of food stalls along Calle 29, known for serving some of the freshest and most affordable seafood in the city. Expect a vibrant, authentic atmosphere and quick service.
picks.whatToOrder: Ceviche de Concha Negra (Black Cockle Ceviche) or Encebollado con Chifles
picks.insiderTip: It's best to go during the day, especially for lunch. Be open to trying different stalls, as each has its loyal following. Carry small bills.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want real Guayaquil seafood, you HAVE to go to Mariscos de la 29. Best encebollado and ceviche for dirt cheap, total local vibe."

picks.name: El Cangrejo Criollo
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For crustacean lovers, El Cangrejo Criollo is the ultimate destination. This specialized restaurant focuses almost exclusively on various preparations of cangrejos (crabs), a beloved Guayaquilean delicacy. The atmosphere is casual and convivial, perfect for digging into a pile of flavorful crabs with friends or family.
picks.whatToOrder: Cangrejos Encocados (Crabs in Coconut Sauce) or Al Ajillo (Garlic Crabs)
picks.insiderTip: They provide mallets and bibs – don't be afraid to get messy! It's an experience best enjoyed with bare hands. Ask about seasonal crab availability.
picks.redditQuote: "El Cangrejo Criollo is THE place for crabs. Get the encocados, they're spicy and delicious. Totally messy but so much fun."

picks.name: Cevicheria Guayaca
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A modern and bright take on the traditional cevichería, Cevicheria Guayaca offers a fresh perspective on classic dishes with excellent presentation. They use high-quality ingredients and offer creative twists on ceviche and other seafood staples. It's a popular spot for both locals and tourists.
picks.whatToOrder: Ceviche de Camarón (Shrimp Ceviche) or Tiradito de Pescado
picks.insiderTip: They often have creative daily specials that are worth trying. Their house-made hot sauces add a great kick to any dish.
picks.redditQuote: "Cevicheria Guayaca has amazing, fresh ceviches. A bit more modern than the street stalls but still super authentic flavors. Great vibe."

picks.name: Lo Nuestro
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the scenic Puerto Santa Ana area, Lo Nuestro offers a sophisticated dining experience with a focus on elevated Ecuadorian cuisine. While not exclusively seafood, their menu features beautifully presented seafood dishes that blend traditional flavors with modern techniques. The riverfront views add to the elegant ambiance.
picks.whatToOrder: Corvina a la Plancha (Grilled Sea Bass) with plantain crust, or Langostinos al Ajillo
picks.insiderTip: Request a table with a view of the Daule River for a more picturesque dining experience, especially around sunset. Great for a romantic dinner.
picks.redditQuote: "Lo Nuestro at Puerto Santa Ana is gorgeous. Had some incredible grilled fish there, super fresh and beautifully plated. A bit pricey but worth it for the view and quality."

picks.name: El Palacio del Encebollado
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As its name suggests, this spot is a temple to Encebollado, Ecuador's beloved fish soup. Locals flock here for their consistently delicious and incredibly satisfying bowls of tuna, yuca, and onion stew. It's a simple, bustling eatery perfect for a quick, hearty breakfast or lunch.
picks.whatToOrder: Encebollado Tradicional (Traditional Encebollado) with a side of chifles (plantain chips)
picks.insiderTip: This is primarily a breakfast and lunch spot, often closing by mid-afternoon. It's a great hangover cure, according to locals!
picks.redditQuote: "If you're in Guayaquil, you MUST get encebollado here. El Palacio del Encebollado is next level. So flavorful and cheap, perfect start to the day."

picks.name: La Canoa (Hotel Continental)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located within the historic Hotel Continental, La Canoa offers a refined yet authentic Ecuadorian dining experience. It's celebrated for its traditional dishes, including a wide selection of expertly prepared seafood. The setting is classic and comfortable, making it a reliable choice for a high-quality meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Arroz con Calamares en su Tinta (Squid in its Ink Rice) or Cazuela de Mariscos
picks.insiderTip: They are famous for their breakfast buffet, which often includes local seafood preparations. It's a great introduction to Ecuadorian cuisine in a comfortable setting.
picks.redditQuote: "Stayed at Hotel Continental and La Canoa was surprisingly good. Their seafood cazuela was incredible, so rich and full of flavor."

picks.name: El Muelle de Darwin
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Inspired by the Galapagos Islands, El Muelle de Darwin offers a unique themed dining experience with a focus on fresh seafood. The decor features maritime elements and nods to Darwin's journey, creating a fun and distinctive atmosphere. It's a great spot for families or anyone looking for more than just a meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Pescado Entero Frito (Whole Fried Fish) or Parrillada de Mariscos (Mixed Seafood Grill)
picks.insiderTip: Their portions are quite generous, so consider sharing if you're not ravenous. Great photo opportunities with the themed decorations.
picks.redditQuote: "El Muelle de Darwin is super cool, especially if you love the Galapagos vibe. Their whole fried fish was amazing, perfectly crispy."

picks.name: La Cevichería de la U
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A bustling and energetic spot popular with university students and locals for its delicious and affordable ceviches. La Cevichería de la U is known for its generous portions, quick service, and vibrant atmosphere. It's a testament to Guayaquil's casual ceviche culture, offering a wide variety of fresh options.
picks.whatToOrder: Ceviche de Pescado (Fish Ceviche) or Bolones de Verde con Queso (Plantain dumplings with cheese)
picks.insiderTip: It can get quite crowded during peak lunch hours due to its popularity with students. Look out for daily lunch specials that offer great value.
picks.redditQuote: "For a cheap and cheerful ceviche fix near the university, La Cevichería de la U is always a winner. Their fish ceviche hits the spot every time."

picks.name: Muelle 12
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located across the river in the upscale Samborondón district, Muelle 12 offers a more contemporary approach to seafood. With stylish decor and beautiful river views, it's a great option for a modern dining experience. Their menu features creative seafood dishes and a selection of fresh sushi, blending local and international influences.
picks.whatToOrder: Tuna Tartare or Langostinos al Coco (Coconut Shrimp)
picks.insiderTip: Samborondón can be a bit of a drive from central Guayaquil, but it's worth it for the ambiance and modern cuisine. Great for an evening out.
picks.redditQuote: "Muelle 12 in Samborondón is fantastic if you want something a bit more upscale and modern. Their tuna tartare was surprisingly good and the view is beautiful."

faq.question: What kind of seafood is Guayaquil known for?
faq.answer: Guayaquil is renowned for its diverse Pacific seafood, primarily fish like tuna and corvina, and shellfish such as shrimp, crab (cangrejo), and black cockles (concha negra). These are often prepared in traditional dishes like ceviche, encebollado, and encocados.

faq.question: What is encebollado and where can I try it?
faq.answer: Encebollado is Ecuador's national dish, a hearty fish stew typically made with fresh tuna, yuca (cassava), and a generous topping of pickled red onions. It's considered a breakfast or lunch staple and a popular hangover cure. You can try authentic encebollado at Pique y Pase or El Palacio del Encebollado.

faq.question: Is it safe to eat street food seafood in Guayaquil?
faq.answer: Generally, yes, but it's important to choose popular, busy stalls where food is prepared fresh and quickly, indicating high turnover. Places like Mariscos de la 29 are iconic and well-regarded by locals for their fresh preparations. Use common sense, observe hygiene, and trust your instincts.

faq.question: What's the typical price range for a seafood meal in Guayaquil?
faq.answer: The price range for seafood in Guayaquil varies widely. You can enjoy a delicious, budget-friendly meal like an encebollado or street ceviche for $5-15. Mid-range restaurants offer full meals for $15-30, while upscale dining experiences can range from $35-60+ per person.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian or non-seafood options available at most seafood restaurants?
faq.answer: While seafood is the specialty, many Guayaquil restaurants, especially larger ones like La Canoa or Lo Nuestro, offer a few non-seafood options, often featuring chicken or beef dishes. However, dedicated vegetarian options might be limited, so it's best to check menus in advance.

faq.question: What's the best time of year to enjoy seafood in Guayaquil?
faq.answer: Guayaquil's climate is tropical year-round, meaning fresh seafood is consistently available. However, the cooler, drier season from May to December might be more comfortable for outdoor dining. Crab season typically peaks during certain months, so inquire locally if you're seeking this specific delicacy.

methodology: Our selection for Guayaquil's best Pacific seafood spots was meticulously curated by local food critics and travel experts. We considered factors like freshness of ingredients, authenticity of preparation, unique ambiance, and overall value, ensuring a diverse range of experiences from casual street eats to upscale dining.
